name: gemma4_31b
status: SECONDARY / EXPERIMENTAL. CPU-tested here: tokenizer (not gated), chat rendering, loss mask, supervised-token counts, LoRA target names and the vLLM key mapping on a meta-device model. NOT run on GPU at all. Expect to debug: multimodal checkpoint class, logit softcapping in the chunked loss, vLLM LoRA on k_eq_v layers, memory with a 262k vocab.
_chat_notes:
Gemma 4 template: '<bos>' + optional '<|turn>system
...<turn|>
' + '<|turn>user
...<turn|>
'. With thinking off the generation prompt is '<|turn>model
<|channel>thought
<channel|>' (an empty thought channel), but the template renders a FINAL assistant message as '<|turn>model
' + content + '<turn|>
' with no thought channel, so the prompt is not a prefix of the full render. render_mode=concat therefore trains on prompt(with generation prompt) + content.strip() + '<turn|>' (supervised) + '
' (masked): exactly the token stream the model sees at evaluation time. Earlier assistant turns in history are rendered by the template without the thought channel.

lora._notes: Regex restricts LoRA to the text decoder: the vision tower also has q_proj/k_proj/... modules (some are Gemma4ClippableLinear, which PEFT cannot wrap). Full-attention layers have no v_proj (attention_k_eq_v=True: V is computed from k_proj).

vllm._lora_notes: Keys are already in the Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration checkpoint convention (base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.*), which vLLM's hf_to_vllm_mapper translates. BUT vLLM loads k_eq_v layers by copying the k_proj base weight into the V slot of qkv_proj and does NOT do the same for LoRA weights, so a k_proj LoRA would change K but not V there, unlike HF. prepare_lora with lora_transform=gemma4_k_eq_v adds v_proj LoRA tensors equal to the k_proj ones on those layers. Verify with the vLLM-vs-HF parity job before trusting any Gemma generation.

expected._note: scripts/golden_render_test.py on the CPU machine, 24 Oct 2026 (tokenizer at the pinned revision)
